extracted.intended_audience: negative option sellers (businesses), compliance officers, in-house and outside counsel, and regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretation and operational compliance with the Federal Trade Commission's final rule concerning negative option programs (the “Click to Cancel” rule), including required disclosures, consent, recordkeeping, and cancellation mechanisms across media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: This Rule contains requirements related to any form of negative option program in any media, including, but not limited to, Interactive Electronic Media, telephone, print, and in-person transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to negative option features in all listed media; scope framing determines which sellers and transactions must comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Billing Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Billing Information means any data that enables any person to access a consumer's account, such as a credit card, checking, savings, share or similar account, utility bill, mortgage loan account, or debit card.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition to identify when the timing requirement 'prior to obtaining the consumer's Billing Information' is triggered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Charge/Charged/Charging
rubrics_metrics.description: Charge, Charged, or Charging means any attempt to collect money or other consideration from a consumer, including but not limited to causing Billing Information to be submitted for payment, including against the consumer's credit card, debit card, bank account, telephone bill, or other account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad definition captures any attempted collection mechanism; important when assessing when consent and disclosure obligations are triggered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Clear and Conspicuous
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear and Conspicuous means that a required disclosure is easily noticeable (i.e., difficult to miss) and easily understandable by ordinary consumers, including in all of the following ways: (1) same means as communication; (2) visual: size/contrast/location/time; (3) audible: volume/speed/cadence sufficient; (4) interactive electronic medium: disclosure must be unavoidable; (5) diction and syntax understandable to ordinary consumers and in each language used in the representation; (6) must comply in each medium through which it is received; (7) must not be contradicted or mitigated by anything else in the communication; (8) when targeting a specific audience, ‘ordinary consumers’ includes that group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains eight specific subrequirements. For interactive electronic communications make disclosures unavoidable; ensure visual/audible attributes make disclosures stand out; avoid contradictory or undermining content; tailor language to audience and languages used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Interactive Electronic Medium
rubrics_metrics.description: Interactive Electronic Medium is any electronic means of communicating (except via telephone calls), including internet, mobile application, text, chat, instant message, email, software, or any online service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggers some specific disclosure/cancellation obligations (e.g., unavoidable disclosures; easy-to-find cancellation mechanisms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Material
rubrics_metrics.description: Material means likely to affect a person's choice of, or conduct regarding, goods or services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to determine which facts must not be misrepresented and which terms must be disclosed prior to obtaining billing information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Negative Option Feature
rubrics_metrics.description: Negative Option Feature is a provision of a contract under which the consumer's silence or failure to take affirmative action to reject a good or service or to cancel the agreement is interpreted by the negative option seller as acceptance or continuing acceptance of the offer, including, but not limited to: (1) an automatic renewal; (2) a continuity plan; (3) a free-to-pay conversion or fee-to-pay conversion; or (4) a pre-notification negative option plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catalog of covered negative option mechanics; use to classify covered offers and determine applicability of disclosure/consent/cancellation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Negative Option Seller
rubrics_metrics.description: Negative Option Seller means the person selling, offering, charging for, or otherwise marketing a good or service with a Negative Option Feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the regulated actor(s) responsible for compliance with the Rule's obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Misrepresentations
rubrics_metrics.description: In connection with promoting or offering for sale any good or service with a Negative Option Feature, it is a violation... for any Negative Option Seller to misrepresent, expressly or by implication, any Material fact, including: (a) the Negative Option Feature or any term of the Negative Option Feature (including consumer consent, any deadline to prevent or stop a Charge, or the cancellation of the Negative Option Feature); (b) Cost; (c) Purpose or efficacy of the underlying good or service; (d) Health or safety; or (e) Any other Material fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad prohibition — covers both express and implied misrepresentations. Use the listed categories as illustrative examples of material facts whose misrepresentation would violate the Rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Disclosures — Timing and Content
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a violation... for a Negative Option Seller to fail to disclose to a consumer, prior to obtaining the consumer's Billing Information, all Material terms, regardless of whether those terms directly relate to the Negative Option Feature, and including but not limited to: (1) That consumers will be Charged or Charges will increase after any trial period and, if applicable, that Charges will be recurring unless consumer timely prevents or stops them; (2) Each deadline (by date or frequency) by which the consumer must act to prevent or stop the Charges; (3) The amount (or range of costs) the consumer will be Charged and, if applicable, the frequency of the Charges; and (4) The information necessary for the consumer to find the simple cancellation mechanism required pursuant to §425.6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All listed disclosures must be provided before billing information is collected. 'All Material terms' is broad—include any terms likely to affect consumer's choice or conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and Content of Required Disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Each disclosure required by paragraph (a) must be Clear and Conspicuous. Placement: (i) disclosures required by (a)(1)-(4) must appear immediately adjacent to the means of recording the consumer's consent; and (ii) disclosures required by paragraph (a) must appear before obtaining the consent required pursuant to §425.5. Other Information: All communications must not contain any other information that interferes with, detracts from, contradicts, or otherwise undermines the ability of consumers to read, hear, see, or otherwise understand the disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure must be simultaneous/adjacent and prior to consent; avoid any surrounding content that undermines comprehension or visibility of disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express Informed Consent Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a violation... for a Negative Option Seller to fail to obtain the consumer's express informed consent before Charging the consumer. In obtaining such express informed consent, the Negative Option Seller must: (1) Obtain the consumer's unambiguously affirmative consent to the Negative Option Feature offer separately from any other portion of the transaction; (2) Not include any information that interferes with, detracts from, contradicts, or otherwise undermines the ability of consumers to provide their express informed consent; and (3) Keep or maintain verification of the consumer's consent for at least three years, except if the seller can demonstrate by a preponderance of the evidence that it uses processes ensuring no consumer can technologically complete the transaction without consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent must be affirmative, separate, non-undermined by other content, and documented for three years unless technological safeguards obviate recordkeeping (burden of proof on seller).

rubrics_metrics.name: Telemarketing Sales Rule (TSR) Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Negative Option Sellers covered by the Telemarketing Sales Rule must comply with all applicable requirements provided in 16 CFR part 310, including, for transactions involving preacquired account information and a free-to-pay-conversion feature, obtaining from the customer, at a minimum, the last four (4) digits of the account number to be charged and making and maintaining an audio recording of the entire telemarketing transaction as required by 16 CFR part 310.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where both the TSR and this Rule apply, sellers must follow the TSR's more specific telemarketing recordkeeping and recording requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation for Written Offers (including internet/phone applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Negative Option Seller will be deemed in compliance for all written offers if that seller obtains the required consent through a check box, signature, or other substantially similar method, which the consumer must affirmatively select or sign to accept the Negative Option Feature and no other portion of the transaction. The consent request must be presented in a manner and format that is clear, unambiguous, non-deceptive, and free of any information not directly related to the consumer's acceptance of the Negative Option Feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checkbox/signature-style consent is acceptable only if presented clearly and free of unrelated material; presentation must not mislead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple Cancellation — Overall Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a violation... for the Negative Option Seller to fail to provide a simple mechanism for a consumer to cancel the Negative Option Feature; avoid being Charged, or Charged an increased amount, for the good or service; and immediately stop any recurring Charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation mechanism must actually stop charges immediately and be easy for consumers to use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple Cancellation — Ease Relative to Consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The simple mechanism required must be at least as easy to use as the mechanism the consumer used to consent to the Negative Option Feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If consent was one-click online, cancellation cannot require additional steps or higher friction (e.g., calling a call center).

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple Cancellation — Minimum Medium and Mode Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Seller must provide the simple mechanism through the same medium the consumer used to consent, and: (1) Interactive Electronic Medium: the mechanism must be easy to find when consumer seeks to cancel; compliance with §425.4(a)(4) does not discharge the obligation; consumer shall not be required to interact with a live or virtual representative (such as a chatbot) to cancel if the consumer did not do so to consent. (2) Telephone call: seller must promptly effectuate cancellations requested via a telephone number that is answered or records messages, made available during normal business hours, and not more costly to use than the telephone call the consumer used to consent. (3) In-person consent: in addition to offering cancellation via similar in-person method where practical, must offer cancellation through an Interactive Electronic Medium or by providing a telephone number; the alternate mechanism must satisfy applicable requirements of (1) and (2) and seller shall not erect a cost-barrier by imposing unnecessary or unreasonable cost for the cancellation call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation must be provided in same medium and (as applicable) be easy-to-find online, not require live agents if not required for consent, and telephone/in-person cancellation must not impose additional costs or barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of Cancellation Information in Disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosures required by paragraph (a)(4) (information necessary for consumer to find the simple cancellation mechanism) must appear immediately adjacent to the means of recording the consumer's consent, and before obtaining consent required under §425.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing a link or buried help page is insufficient if cancellation information is not adjacent/visible at the point of consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to State Laws
rubrics_metrics.description: This part shall not be construed as superseding, altering, or affecting any State statute, regulation, order, or interpretation relating to negative option requirements, except to the extent it is inconsistent with the provisions of this part. A State statute/regulation/order/interpretation is not inconsistent if it affords any consumer greater protection than provided under this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal rule displaces state law only to the extent of inconsistency; states may provide greater protections without conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions — Petition Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person to whom this part applies may petition the Commission for a partial or full exemption. The Commission may issue partial or full exemptions if it finds application of this part's requirements is not necessary to prevent the acts or practices to which this part relates. The Commission shall resolve petitions using procedures provided in 16 CFR 1.31 and may condition exemptions on compliance with alternative standards prescribed by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is an administrative path for relief; exemptions may be conditional and are discretionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of this part are separate and severable from one another. If any provision is stayed or determined to be invalid, the remaining provisions shall continue in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal protection that surviving provisions remain enforceable even if part of the Rule is invalidated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping, Retention, and PRA-related Findings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission curtailed retention to only three years for records of consent; sellers must keep verification of consent for at least three years unless they can demonstrate by a preponderance of the evidence that processes ensure no consumer can technologically complete the transaction without consent. The Commission also assessed PRA burdens and adopted estimates (e.g., 106,000 entities; 53,000 recordkeeping burden hours (1 hour per entity per year); 212,000 disclosure hours (2 hours per seller per year)) and labor cost estimates for annual compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retention requirement is limited to three years unless the technological-safeharbor is proven; PRA analysis provides the Commission's expected compliance burden/cost estimates which may be useful for compliance planning and internal cost accounting.
